items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: That was a girl vocalist with the group. Her name was Linda something, I don't know, and she liked me, you know.

ctx.x: Oh, boy, oh, boy. Well, I'll give you an idea. I was in a little town, Rosedale we stopped, and I went into a little place to get a sandwich, so there was an old white man in there, and there was just the two of us. Nobody -- as a matter of fact no one was in there but him, and I went in and I ordered a ham sandwich, and I think a pork sandwich, and he started cutting the meat, slowly, you know. He was very -- I could see him thinking, I could see the wheels turning. This was an old man. So he finally just stuck…

That was a girl vocalist with the group. Her name was Linda something, I don't know, and she liked me, you know. So we played a town called Tupelo, Mississippi, and this girl had to -- she was a very attractive girl, she was a mulatto girl, you know, very light. And she had to send a telegram or something and she wanted me to walk down town with her, so

we -- I've walked, and on our way back there were a car full of white guys and they would drive along and just as we were going to cross the intersection they would stop and park in front of us and we would have to walk around the car. And they were making all kind of remarks, you know.
